Definition: properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphemistically, but rarely) to reprove
BiblicalUsage: Chacad means to be kind, to show mercy — and, strangely, it can also mean to be put to shame. David sings it twice over: with the merciful God will show Himself merciful. Proverbs uses the other edge of it, warning that a man who betrays a secret will be put to shame and his infamy will not turn away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mercy is the shape of God's dealings: He shows Himself merciful to the merciful, and the man who shows no mercy finds shame waiting for him. The shame in Proverbs is the other side of the same coin: mercy withheld turns to disgrace.
